clue.text: H, perhaps, in the role of buccaneer?

definitions.note: a noun: the letter H stands for the breathy sound, an example of the class

parts.note: 'as' means acting in the role of, as in 'appearing as Hamlet'
a buccaneer is a pirate

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what part the letter H might play in a pirate story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'H, perhaps' looks like a letter used in the wordplay, but it is the definition, flagged as an example by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an aspirate is a breathed consonant sound, and H is the standard instance.

clue.text: Area used to be hot and seriously flooded

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A district that was once sweltering is now under water.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered with water, swamped.

clue.text: Possible earl in Gateshead, having a close look

parts.note: an earl is one kind of peer, a member of the nobility
read as gate's head: the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A man who may be an earl is spotted scrutinising something in a north-east England town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead, a town near Newcastle, splits as 'Gate's head', its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely or searchingly, so peering is staring intently.

clue.text: Fearful, but again subject to uncertainty?

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
doubtable means open to doubt

explanation.surface: Something alarming that, on reflection, may be questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fearful' here means inspiring fear, not afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubtable means formidable, worthy of being feared or respected.

clue.text: Groovy attempt to secure goal

indicators.note: 'to secure' means to hold fast, so the word for attempt wraps round the word for goal

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A cool attempt at scoring in a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Groovy is dated slang for fashionable, which is what trendy means.

clue.text: Diving duck scared at first by cat's cry

indicators.note: 'at first' asks for only the opening letter of the word scared

parts.note: a mew is the cry a cat makes

explanation.surface: A duck plunges underwater, startled by a cat mewing at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small sawbill duck that feeds by diving for fish.

clue.text: Molten rock mother observed around foot of berg

indicators.note: 'around' has the word for mother surrounding the letter that follows

parts.note: mama is a word for mother

indicators.note: 'foot of' in a down clue means the last letter of berg

explanation.surface: A mother watches lava flow round the base of an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts G, the foot of 'berg', inside MAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is the molten material beneath the earth's crust that becomes lava.

clue.text: Worrying at first, a phase in degeneration

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of the word worrying

parts.note: a stage is a phase

explanation.surface: An alarming period in the course of a decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is loss through decay or gradual decline.

clue.text: Unseen, a badger tormented a bovine animal

definitions.note: noun phrase matching the breed name

indicators.note: something tormented is twisted and distorted, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone, out of sight, harasses a badger and then a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like a verb meaning pester, but it is only anagram fodder; 'tormented' twists all thirteen letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of beef cattle, so one is a member of the cow family.

clue.text: Youth in case once led astray

indicators.note: 'astray' means off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A young person wrongly guided in a particular case long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led' belongs to the fodder; only 'astray' signals the anagram of CASE ONCE LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescence is the period of youth between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Japanese verse originally hidden away in Kyoto university

indicators.note: 'originally' asks for the starting letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A Japanese poem has been tucked away somewhere in a Kyoto university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' suggests a hidden word, but it is just one of the words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines and seventeen syllables.

clue.text: Three-dimensional scene Ivor regularly included in play

indicators.note: 'included in' places the picked letters inside the word for a play

parts.note: a play is a drama

indicators.note: 'regularly' takes every other letter of the name Ivor, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tableau featuring Ivor keeps turning up in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes I and O from IVOR, which are 'included in' DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a model display that shows a scene in miniature with depth.

clue.text: Drunk son's inappropriate garment?

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's simply attaches the garment to him

explanation.surface: A tipsy son is wearing something unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is playful: hosiery on a son is the 'inappropriate garment' imagined.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are close-fitting leg wear usually associated with women, hence unsuitable for a son.

clue.text: Time to walk with swinging motion? Nonsense

parts.note: to waddle is to walk swaying from side to side

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a moment to walk with a rolling gait.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, trivial talk or writing, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: Stick one's nose in, hearing gong

indicators.note: 'hearing' tells us the answer is a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: Someone poking into others' business while listening for a gong to sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' suggests a percussion instrument, but in British slang it is a medal, which is said just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere in matters that are not your concern is to pry, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Dedicated action inspiring five religious books

indicators.note: 'inspiring' means breathing in, so the word for action takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: a deed is an action
V is the Roman numeral for five
OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: A committed act that motivates five scriptural volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted and dedicated both mean wholeheartedly committed.

clue.text: Old way the French primarily regarded a stableman

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
le is French for the

indicators.note: 'primarily' takes the first letter of the word regarded

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned French view of someone who tends horses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was a groom at an inn who looked after travellers' horses.

clue.text: Live among opponents in French resort

indicators.note: 'among' places the word for live inside the word for opponents

parts.note: antis are people opposed to something
to be is to exist, i.e. live

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to dwell amid enemies on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a seaside town on the Côte d'Azur between Cannes and Nice.

clue.text: Symbol adopted by Vladivostok entrepreneurs

indicators.note: 'adopted by' means taken in by the words that follow, which contain the answer

explanation.surface: Businesspeople in a Russian Pacific port take on an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or emblem standing for something else.

clue.text: Group of witches beginning to clean stove

indicators.note: 'beginning to' takes only the opening letter of the word clean

parts.note: an oven is part of a stove, a kitchen cooker

explanation.surface: The witches start scrubbing their stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, traditionally thirteen.

clue.text: Woman in US city, one looking after children

indicators.note: 'in' places the woman's name inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in New York working as a childminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a person employed to care for children in a family home.

clue.text: Noble old general giving up whiskey for jazzman

parts.note: a duke is a nobleman

indicators.note: 'giving up' says a letter is surrendered from the general's name

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington was the British general who beat Napoleon at Waterloo
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An aristocratic veteran officer quits drinking and takes up jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' drops W (whiskey in radio code) from WELLINGTON, leaving ELLINGTON. 'whiskey' looks like the drink being renounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was the celebrated American jazz bandleader, composer and pianist.

clue.text: Reportedly bring in bird of prey

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as it is said, so the answer sounds like the next word

parts.note: to bring in money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone is bringing a raptor indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large raptor.

clue.text: Amiable, and at close of day extremely lively

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
the close of something is its end

indicators.note: 'extremely' takes the outermost letters of the word lively

explanation.surface: Someone pleasant who becomes wildly animated as evening falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs in answer order: FRI (day) then END (close), then LY from the ends of 'lively'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being friendly means being genial and warm toward others.
